title: Indian-American Google Executive Sheetal Wrzesien Shot Dead by Husband in Georgia
excerpt: Sheetal Wrzesien, 57, a former Google engineering leader and Georgia Tech alumna, was fatally shot at her Cobb County home on July 7. Her husband Kirk B. Wrzesien faces felony murder charges.
body:
• Sheetal Wrzesien, 57, a former Google engineering leader, was shot dead at her home in Smyrna, Georgia, on July 7, 2026
  • Her husband Kirk B. Wrzesien, 56, was arrested at the scene and faces five felony charges, including felony murder
  • The couple's 23-year-old son Jason was also shot but survived after fleeing to a neighbor's house for help
  • Wrzesien had over 20 years of experience in tech, held two software patents, and served on Georgia Tech's College of Computing advisory board

Sheetal Wrzesien, a 57-year-old Indian-American technology executive and former Google engineering leader, was shot and killed at her home in Cobb County, Georgia, on the evening of July 7, 2026. Her husband, 56-year-old Kirk B. Wrzesien, was arrested at the scene and is being held without bond at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center, according to the Cobb County Police Department.

What Happened on Laurel Creek Trail

Officers responded to reports of gunfire at the family's residence on Laurel Creek Trail in Smyrna, a suburb of Atlanta, shortly before 8 p.m. on Tuesday. When police arrived, they found the couple's 23-year-old son, Jason Wrzesien, outside the house with critical gunshot injuries. Despite being wounded, Jason had managed to flee the residence and reach a neighbor's home to call for help, according to LatestLY.

Inside the home, officers found Sheetal Wrzesien with multiple gunshot wounds. She was pronounced dead at the scene. Jason was rushed to a local hospital, where he underwent emergency surgery. Authorities later indicated his injuries were not believed to be life-threatening, though his current condition has not been publicly updated.

The Cobb County Police Department said the shooting stemmed from an escalating domestic confrontation within the household, according to Fox News. Kirk Wrzesien was taken into custody without incident.

Five Felony Charges Filed

According to court documents, Kirk Wrzesien faces five felony charges: one count of felony murder, two counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon — one each for the attacks on his wife and son — and two counts of possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony. He remains held without bond. No additional suspects are being sought.

"I've seen him doing yard work. Really nice guy. Very social neighbour. It's a terrible tragedy."

— Peter Lee, neighbor, speaking to Atlanta News First

Neighbors on Laurel Creek Trail expressed shock at the violence. Joanne Anderson, who has lived on the street for over 20 years, told Atlanta News First she had no warning. "I didn't know what was going on. I didn't know if someone had a heart attack or what had happened," she said.

A Distinguished Career in Technology

Sheetal Wrzesien grew up across England, India, and Ghana before moving to the United States to study computer science at the Georgia Institute of Technology, graduating in 1994. She built a career spanning more than two decades in the technology sector, working at some of America's largest companies.

At Google, she served as Head of Marketing Technology and as Engineering and Operations Lead for data governance, content management, and CRM systems. She later returned to Google as a Marketing Technology Advisor in the Android division, according to her LinkedIn profile. Before Google, she led mobile and digital transformation at The Home Depot, helping the retailer become one of the most successful e-commerce companies in the United States.

Wrzesien was a named inventor on two software patents, served on the advisory board of Georgia Tech's College of Computing, and sat on the Board of Trustees for the Georgia Tech Alumni Association. She was also a fellow of the Aspen Institute's Tech Policy Hub. At the time of her death, she was working as Senior Director at GoTo Foods, according to World Malayalee Voice.

Diaspora Community in Mourning

Wrzesien's death has sent shockwaves through the Indian-American community in Atlanta and the broader diaspora. She was widely recognized for mentoring young professionals and championing women in STEM fields, sponsoring and guiding women in technical roles for over a decade.

The case has also renewed attention to domestic violence within immigrant and professional communities in the United States. Advocacy groups have urged anyone experiencing domestic abuse to contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233.

Investigation Ongoing

Authorities have confirmed the investigation remains focused on what they described as an isolated domestic incident. The motive behind the shooting has not been publicly disclosed. No further arrests are expected.

Sheetal Wrzesien is survived by her two children, Jason and Jessica.
